title: U.S. House · West Virginia's 1st District
area: West Virginia's 1st Congressional District, covering the northern and eastern parts of the state including Huntington and Morgantown.

context.text: Incumbent Carol Miller (R) defeated Larry Jackson in the Republican primary on May 12, 2026 with 72.0% of the vote. Vince George defeated Britta Aguirre in the Democratic primary with 53.0% of the vote.

candidates.name: Carol Miller
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 12 Republican primary with 72.0% of the vote

positions.summary: In a February 4, 2025 Newsmax interview summarized in her office's press release, she backed President Trump's plan to place tariffs on Canada and China, saying he is bringing those countries to the table and tying the effort to securing the border.

record.text: Assigned to the House Committee on Ways and Means, including its Health and Trade subcommittees, for the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: Vince George
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 12 Democratic primary with 53.0% of the vote

priorities.text: "Making life affordable for working West Virginians is my top priority. I support fully funding SNAP, Social Security, and veterans' benefits, and I oppose harmful funding cuts to safety net programs."
"Medicare For All &/or a single payer public option in which no person is left without health & medical coverage."
"More than doubling the Federal minimum wage to at least $15 per hour for all workers, expansion of eligibility & benefits for Social Security participants."

positions.summary: Supports Medicare for All or a single-payer public option covering everyone.
positions.quote: Medicare For All &/or a single payer public option in which no person is left without health & medical coverage.

positions.summary: Supports more than doubling the federal minimum wage to at least $15 per hour.
positions.quote: More than doubling the Federal minimum wage to at least $15 per hour for all workers.

positions.summary: His campaign site says immigration enforcement is important and also that ICE is violating people's rights and he will fight due-process violations.
positions.quote: Immigration enforcement is important. But ICE is violating people’s rights, engaging in federal overreach, and encroaching on West Virginia’s local communities.

statements.quote: I’ll fight to make childcare more affordable and strengthen rural public transit systems.
I also believe in a free market that allows renewable energy to expand in West Virginia if that’s what businesses want to do.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions from his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey and his campaign Platform page; his page does not address abortion, guns, taxes or tariffs.

candidates.name: Belinda Fox-Spencer

priorities.text: A 2022 campaign website statement listed education as a priority, citing high child poverty rates in West Virginia as a barrier to educational quality.

candidates.researchNotes: Statements are her own written answers to the 2026 iVoterGuide questionnaire (iVoterGuide is run by AFA Action, a partisan organization; only her verbatim wording is used, not the agree/disagree ratings).
